page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-16 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 server family. It features 16 virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled, running on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 128 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. The underlying Intel processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and 8-bit integer operations. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the n4-highmem-16 demonstrates balanced compute and memory performance. The instance achieved a single-core stress-ng CPU score of 1563.58 and a multi-core score of 12846.34. Memory subsystem performance is characterized by a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 1084.69 GB/sec, which drops to 115.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and a write bandwidth of 66.19 GB/sec. Database operations are supported by a Passmark database score of 7313.73 and a Redis SET throughput of 17.18 million operations per second. For specialized workloads, the CPU's AMX instructions enable small-model (135M) LLM inference prompt processing at 1277.73 tokens per second, though performance scales down to 10.32 tokens per second for larger 70B models.

The resource profile of the n4-highmem-16 presents specific architectural tradeoffs. The absence of local SSD storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-intensive applications requiring sub-millisecond local latency. Similarly, the lack of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though the integrated AMX instructions offer a CPU-based alternative for lighter inference tasks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density relative to the vCPU count makes this instance suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require proportional scaling of compute cores. Recommended workloads include in-memory databases, caching layers, software compilation, and data processing tasks that fit within the 128 GB memory envelope.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-16 is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance featuring 16 vCPUs (8 physical Intel cores) and 128 GB of RAM, providing 8 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. It lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. In benchmarks, the instance delivers a multi-core stress-ng score of 12846.34, a Redis SET throughput of 17.18 million operations per second, and a cached memory read bandwidth of 1084.69 GB/sec. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it a cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high compute-to-RAM scaling. It is well-suited for in-memory databases, caching layers, software compilation, and light CPU-based machine learning inference.
